title.zh: 卷260 列傳四十七 姚启圣 吴兴祚 施琅
title.en: Volume 260 Biographies 47: Yao Qisheng, Wu Xingzuo, Shi Lang
title.raw: 卷260 列傳四十七 姚启圣 吴兴祚 施琅

sentences.zh: 姚啟聖，字熙止，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Yao Qisheng, courtesy name Xizhi, was a man of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Qisheng, whose courtesy name was Xizhi, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少任俠自喜。

translations.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he lived by the code of the knight-errant and took pride in his own daring.

sentences.zh: 明季為諸生。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming he was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Ming dynasty he held the rank of licentiate.

sentences.zh: 順治初，師定江南，遊通州，為土豪所侮，乃詣軍前乞自效。

translations.literal: In the early Shunzhi reign, when the armies pacified Jiangnan, he traveled to Tongzhou and was insulted by a local bully; he then went to the army camp to offer his services.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign, while the Qing armies were pacifying the Jiangnan region, he was traveling in Tongzhou when a local bully humiliated him; he went straight to the army headquarters and asked to serve.

sentences.zh: 檄署通州知州，執土豪杖殺之，棄官歸。

translations.literal: By order he was appointed acting prefect of Tongzhou; he seized the bully, had him beaten to death with the cudgel, and resigned his office.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as acting prefect of Tongzhou, seized the bully, had him clubbed to death, and then resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 郊行，遇二卒掠女子，故與好語，奪其刀殺之，還女子其家。

translations.literal: While traveling in the suburbs he met two soldiers robbing a woman; he spoke kindly to them on purpose, snatched their swords and killed them, and returned the woman to her family.
translations.idiomatic: Once on an outing beyond the city walls he came upon two soldiers abducting a woman; he spoke to them pleasantly on purpose, seized their blades and killed them, and sent the woman back to her family.

sentences.zh: 去附族人，籍隸鑲紅旗漢軍。

translations.literal: He left to join kinsmen and was registered in the Hanjun of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He went to live with kinsmen and was entered on the registers of the Han Bannermen of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 舉康熙二年八旗鄉試第一，授廣東香山知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he placed first in the Eight Banners provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Xiangshan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Kangxi reign he took first place in the Eight Banners provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Xiangshan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 前政負課數万，繫獄，啟聖牒大府，悉為代償。

translations.literal: His predecessor owed tens of thousands in taxes and was imprisoned; Qisheng petitioned the provincial authorities and paid the whole sum on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had left tens of thousands in unpaid taxes and lay in prison; Qisheng petitioned the provincial authorities and paid the entire debt himself.

sentences.zh: 尋以擅開海禁，被劾奪官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was impeached and dismissed for opening the maritime ban without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was impeached and stripped of office for having opened the maritime trade ban on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠反，兵入浙江境，陷溫​​州傍近及台、處諸屬縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled; his troops entered Zhejiang and captured Wenzhou and nearby areas as well as the dependent counties of Taizhou and Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rose in rebellion; his forces crossed into Zhejiang, seized the districts around Wenzhou, and overran the subordinate counties of Taizhou and Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 聖祖命康親王杰書統師進討，啟聖與子儀募健兒數百詣軍，以策幹王。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor ordered Prince Kang Jieshu to command the army in a punitive expedition; Qisheng and his son Yi raised several hundred stalwart men and came to the army with stratagems to advise the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor ordered Prince Kang Jieshu to take command of a punitive expedition; Qisheng and his son Yi recruited several hundred sturdy fighters and came to the camp to offer the prince their counsel.

sentences.zh: 檄署諸暨知縣，剿平紫瑯山土寇。

translations.literal: By order he was appointed acting magistrate of Zhuji and suppressed the bandits on Mount Zilang.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he was made acting magistrate of Zhuji and wiped out the local bandits on Mount Zilang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以王薦，超擢溫處道僉事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, on the prince's recommendation, he was promoted in exceptional rank to surveillance commissioner of Wenzhou and Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, on the prince's recommendation, he was promoted by special exception to surveillance commissioner of the Wenzhou and Chuzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 從都統拉哈達克松陽、宣平二縣。

translations.literal: He followed the commandant-in-chief Lahadak and recovered the two counties of Songyang and Xuanping.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the commandant-in-chief Lahadak and recovered the counties of Songyang and Xuanping.

sentences.zh: 十五年，偕副都統沃申、總兵陳世凱等勦賊石塘，焚其木城，斬獲甚眾，乘勝復云和。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, together with the deputy commandant-in-chief Wo Shen, regional commander Chen Shikai, and others, he attacked the rebels at Shitang, burned their wooden fort, killed and captured a great many, and taking advantage of victory recovered Yunhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, together with the deputy commandant-in-chief Wo Shen, regional commander Chen Shikai, and others, he attacked the rebels at Shitang, burned their wooden fortress, killed and captured a great many of them, and pressed the advantage to retake Yunhe.

sentences.zh: 先是，精忠以書招鄭錦，錦至复拒之，將士多為內應，錦遂取泉、漳二府，據廈門。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jingzhong had sent a letter to recruit Zheng Jing; when Jing arrived Jingzhong again refused him, but many officers and men acted as internal collaborators, so Jing took Quanzhou and Zhangzhou and held Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jingzhong had written to summon Zheng Jing; when Jing arrived Jingzhong turned him away again, but many officers and men served as inside collaborators, and Jing thereupon seized the prefectures of Quanzhou and Zhangzhou and held Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 精忠與戰，复屢敗。

translations.literal: Jingzhong fought with him but was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong fought him but was beaten again and again.

sentences.zh: 啟聖又使儀破精忠將曾養性於溫州。

translations.literal: Qisheng again had Yi defeat Jingzhong's general Zeng Yangxing at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng again sent Yi to defeat Jingzhong's general Zeng Yangxing at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，師入仙霞關，趨福建，精忠降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the army entered Xianxia Pass and marched on Fujian; Jingzhong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army passed through Xianxia Pass and advanced into Fujian; Jingzhong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 擢啟聖福建布政使，率兵討錦。

translations.literal: Qisheng was promoted to Fujian provincial administration commissioner and led troops to attack Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng was promoted to Fujian provincial administration commissioner and led troops against Zheng Jing.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂將韓大任驍勇善戰，世稱小淮陰者也，自贛入汀，謀與錦合。

translations.literal: Han Daren, a general of Wu Sangui, was famed for valor in battle and was called by his contemporaries "the lesser Huaiyin"; he came from Gan into Ting and planned to join forces with Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren, a general under Wu Sangui, was famed for his fighting prowess and was known in his day as "the lesser Huaiyin"; he came from Ganzhou into Tingzhou intending to join forces with Zheng Jing.

sentences.zh: 啟聖說之降，簡其部卒，得死士三千人，以為親軍。

translations.literal: Qisheng persuaded him to surrender, selected men from his troops, and obtained three thousand death-defying soldiers whom he made his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng persuaded him to surrender, picked men from his ranks, and formed a personal guard of three thousand men willing to die for him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，從康親王復邵武、興化，盡取漳、泉地。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he followed Prince Kang and recovered Shaowu and Xinghua, taking all the territory of Zhangzhou and Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he followed Prince Kang in recovering Shaowu and Xinghua and took all the territory of Zhangzhou and Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 錦遁歸廈門。

translations.literal: Jing fled back to Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing fled back to Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 總督郎廷佐奏啟聖與子儀屢著戰功，贍軍購馬，具甲胄弓矢，糜白金五萬，皆出私財，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Governor-general Lang Tingzuo memorialized that Qisheng and his son Yi had repeatedly distinguished themselves in battle, supplied the army and purchased horses, and provided armor, bows and arrows at a cost of fifty thousand taels of pure silver, all from private funds; the emperor praised and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Lang Tingzuo reported that Qisheng and his son Yi had repeatedly distinguished themselves in battle, provisioned the army, bought horses, and furnished armor, bows, and arrows at a cost of fifty thousand taels of pure silver—all from their own purses—and the court praised and rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 十七年，錦遣其將劉國軒、吳淑、阿佑等復犯漳、泉，海澄公黃芳世、都統穆赫林、提督段應舉等與戰，敗績，遂陷海澄、長泰、同安、惠安、平和諸縣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jing sent his generals Liu Guoxuan, Wu Shu, Ayoo, and others to attack Zhangzhou and Quanzhou again; the Prince of Haicheng Huang Fangshi, commandant-in-chief Mu Helin, provincial military commissioner Duan Yingju, and others fought them but were defeated, and Haicheng, Changtai, Tong'an, Huian, Pinghe, and other counties were lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zheng Jing sent his generals Liu Guoxuan, Wu Shu, Ayoo, and others to strike again at Zhangzhou and Quanzhou; the Prince of Haicheng Huang Fangshi, commandant-in-chief Mu Helin, provincial military commissioner Duan Yingju, and others met them in battle but were routed, and Haicheng, Changtai, Tong'an, Huian, Pinghe, and other counties fell.

sentences.zh: 詔擢啟聖福建總督，條上機宜，「請調福寧鎮兵助攻泉州，調衢州、贛州、潮州三鎮兵助攻漳州，復設漳浦、同安二總兵，增督標兵五千。

translations.literal: By edict Qisheng was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and presented a detailed plan, "requesting that troops of Funing garrison be moved to assist the attack on Quanzhou, that troops of Quzhou, Ganzhou, and Chaozhou garrisons assist the attack on Zhangzhou, that zonal commanders be reestablished at Zhangpu and Tong'an, and that five thousand troops be added to the governor-general's standard.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Qisheng was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and laid out a detailed plan: "I request that troops from the Funing garrison be shifted to assist the attack on Quanzhou, that troops from the Quzhou, Ganzhou, and Chaozhou garrisons assist the attack on Zhangzhou, that zonal commanders be reestablished at Zhangpu and Tong'an, and that five thousand men be added to the governor-general's personal standard.

sentences.zh: 通省經制兵萬八千，申明臨陣賞罰，禁廝役佔兵額」。

translations.literal: Provincial regular troops number eighteen thousand; rewards and punishments on campaign are to be made clear, and camp servants occupying military quotas are forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: The province's regular troops total eighteen thousand; rewards and punishments in the field should be made explicit, and camp servants must be forbidden from occupying military quotas."

sentences.zh: 下議政王大臣議，衢、贛、潮三路皆重地，未便徵發，既增督標兵，毋庸复廣通省兵額，餘皆從其議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the council of princes and great ministers for discussion; the three routes of Qu, Gan, and Chao were all important posts and could not conveniently be mobilized; since standard troops for the governor-general had already been increased, there was no need to expand provincial quotas further—the rest was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was sent to the council of princes and great ministers; the Quzhou, Ganzhou, and Chaozhou routes were all vital posts and could not conveniently be stripped of troops; since the governor-general's standard had already been enlarged, there was no need to raise the province-wide troop quota further—and the rest of his plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 七月，偕海澄公黃芳度自永福進克平和、漳平。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, together with the Prince of Haicheng Huang Fangdu, he advanced from Yongfu and recovered Pinghe and Zhangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, together with the Prince of Haicheng Huang Fangdu, he advanced from Yongfu and retook Pinghe and Zhangping.

sentences.zh: 國軒等解泉州圍，進逼漳州，壁於蜈蚣嶺。

translations.literal: Guoxuan and others lifted the siege of Quanzhou and pressed toward Zhangzhou, encamping at Wugong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan and his fellows raised the siege of Quanzhou and pressed toward Zhangzhou, where they fortified themselves on Wugong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 啟聖率壯士鍾寶、張黑子等出戰，將軍賚塔、都統沃申等夾擊，連破賊寨，斬其將鄭英、劉正璽等十餘人，國軒遁海澄，乘勝复長泰。

translations.literal: Qisheng led stalwarts Zhong Bao, Zhang Heizi, and others into battle; General Sagui, commandant-in-chief Wo Shen, and others attacked from both sides, broke rebel camps in succession, killed more than ten of their generals including Zheng Ying and Liu Zhengxi, Guoxuan fled to Haicheng, and they took advantage to recover Changtai.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng led his stalwarts Zhong Bao, Zhang Heizi, and others into battle; General Sagui, commandant-in-chief Wo Shen, and others struck from both flanks, broke one rebel camp after another, and killed more than ten of their generals including Zheng Ying and Liu Zhengxi; Guoxuan fled to Haicheng, and they pressed on to retake Changtai.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進正一品。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was reckoned he was advanced to the first rank.

sentences.zh: 九月，復遣儀率兵攻同安，敵棄城遁，斬其將林欽等。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again sent Yi to lead troops against Tong'an; the enemy abandoned the city and fled, and their generals Lin Qin and others were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he again sent Yi to lead troops against Tong'an; the enemy abandoned the city and fled, and generals such as Lin Qin were killed.

sentences.zh: 尋偕副都統吉勒塔布、提督楊捷等進攻海澄，敗國軒於江東橋，又敗之於潮溝。

translations.literal: Soon he joined deputy commandant-in-chief Jiletabu, provincial military commissioner Yang Jie, and others in attacking Haicheng, defeating Guoxuan at Jiangdong Bridge and again at Chaogou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined deputy commandant-in-chief Jiletabu, provincial military commissioner Yang Jie, and others in attacking Haicheng, defeating Guoxuan at Jiangdong Bridge and again at Chaogou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，國軒與淑、佑等踞郭塘、歐溪頭，欲斷江東橋以犯長泰。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan, Shu, Ayoo, and others held Gedang and Ouxitou and intended to cut Jiangdong Bridge to threaten Changtai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan, Shu, Ayoo, and others held Gedang and Ouxitou and planned to sever Jiangdong Bridge in order to strike at Changtai.

sentences.zh: 啟聖偕賚塔、捷及巡撫吳興祚等邀擊，大敗之，先後招降所置吏四百餘、兵一萬四千有奇。

translations.literal: Qisheng joined Sagui, Jie, and governor Wu Xingzuo in intercepting them and inflicted a great defeat; in succession they induced more than four hundred officials and over fourteen thousand troops whom the enemy had appointed to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng joined Sagui, Jie, and Governor Wu Xingzuo in intercepting them and inflicted a crushing defeat; in succession they induced more than four hundred officials and over fourteen thousand troops whom the enemy had installed to surrender.

sentences.zh: 國軒等復率萬餘人謀奪榴山寨，啟聖偕賚塔及副都統石調聲擊敗之，至太平橋、潮溝，斬千餘級。

translations.literal: Guoxuan and others again led more than ten thousand men in a bid to seize Liushan Stockade; Qisheng joined Sagui and deputy commandant-in-chief Shi Diaosheng to defeat them; at Taiping Bridge and Chaogou more than a thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan and others again led more than ten thousand men in an attempt to seize Liushan Stockade; Qisheng joined Sagui and deputy commandant-in-chief Shi Diaosheng to defeat them; at Taiping Bridge and Chaogou more than a thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 十九年，會賚塔等攻海澄。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he joined Sagui and others in attacking Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he joined Sagui and others in the attack on Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 時提督萬正色先克海壇，啟聖及總兵趙得壽、黃大來等分兵七路並進，破十九寨；

translations.literal: At that time provincial military commissioner Wan Zhengse had first taken Haitan; Qisheng and regional commanders Zhao Deshou, Huang Dalai, and others advanced in seven columns and broke nineteen stockades;
translations.idiomatic: By then provincial military commissioner Wan Zhengse had already taken Haitan; Qisheng and regional commanders Zhao Deshou, Huang Dalai, and others advanced in seven columns and stormed nineteen stockades;

sentences.zh: 別遣將渡海，拔金門、廈門，降錦將朱天貴等，錦退保澎湖，盡复所陷郡縣：進兵部尚書、太子太保。

translations.literal: separately he sent generals across the sea to take Jinmen and Xiamen and induced Jing's general Zhu Tiangui and others to surrender; Jing withdrew to defend Penghu, and all lost prefectures and counties were recovered: he was promoted to minister of war and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: he separately sent generals across the sea to take Jinmen and Xiamen and induced Zheng Jing's general Zhu Tiangui and others to surrender; Zheng Jing withdrew to hold Penghu, and all the prefectures and counties that had fallen were recovered—whereupon Qisheng was promoted to minister of war and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十年，左都御史徐元文劾「啟聖疏請借司庫銀十二萬，經營取息，侵占民利；

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Left Censor-in-chief Xu Yuanwen impeached him, stating "Qisheng memorialized requesting to borrow 120,000 taels from the treasury for investment to earn interest, encroaching on the people's profit;
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the left censor-in-chief Xu Yuanwen impeached him, charging that "Qisheng memorialized asking to borrow 120,000 taels from the treasury to invest for profit, encroaching on the people's gain;

sentences.zh: 題報軍前捐銀十五萬，皆剋軍餉朘民膏而得。

translations.literal: in reports of donations at the front of 150,000 taels, all were obtained by deducting military pay and draining the people's fat.
translations.idiomatic: in reporting donations at the front of 150,000 taels, all of it was obtained by skimming military pay and draining the people's substance.

sentences.zh: 閩民極困，啟聖不能存撫，拆毀民居，築園亭水閣，日役千人，舞女歌兒充牣房闥；

translations.literal: The people of Fujian are extremely distressed; Qisheng cannot preserve and comfort them—he demolishes people's houses to build gardens and pavilions over water, employing a thousand men daily; singing girls and dancers fill the rooms and halls;
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian are in extreme distress, yet Qisheng cannot preserve and comfort them—he tears down private homes to build gardens and waterside pavilions, employing a thousand men a day, and singing girls and dancers crowd every room and hall;

sentences.zh: 又強取長泰戴氏女為妾。

translations.literal: he also forcibly took the daughter of the Dai family of Changtai as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: he also forcibly took a daughter of the Dai family of Changtai as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 海壇進師，力為阻撓，及克廈門，又言當直取台灣。

translations.literal: When the army advanced on Haitan he vigorously obstructed it, and after Xiamen was taken he said they should attack Taiwan directly.
translations.idiomatic: When the army advanced on Haitan he did all he could to obstruct it, and after Xiamen was taken he argued that Taiwan should be taken at once.

sentences.zh: 始欲養寇，繼欲窮兵。

translations.literal: At first he wished to nurture the bandits, then he wished to exhaust the army.
translations.idiomatic: At first he wished to let the rebels thrive; afterward he wished to exhaust the army.

sentences.zh: 吳興祚、萬正色平海奏功，啟聖慚妒，妄謂正色與錦將朱天貴有約，讓海壇而去。

translations.literal: When Wu Xingzuo and Wan Zhengse reported merit for pacifying the sea, Qisheng was ashamed and jealous and falsely claimed that Zhengse had an agreement with Jing's general Zhu Tiangui and yielded Haitan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xingzuo and Wan Zhengse reported their merit in pacifying the sea, Qisheng, ashamed and jealous, falsely claimed that Zhengse had a secret agreement with Zheng Jing's general Zhu Tiangui and had yielded Haitan.

sentences.zh: 險詐欺誣，乞敕部嚴議」。

translations.literal: Deceitful, treacherous, and fraudulent—begging that the ministry be ordered to deliberate severely."
translations.idiomatic: He is treacherous, deceitful, and fraudulent—I beg that the ministry be ordered to deliberate on him with the utmost severity."

sentences.zh: 上令啟聖覆奏，啟聖言：「臣於康熙十七年十月進兵至鳳凰山，因一時投誠者多，犒賞不繼，與撫臣吳興祚議外省貿易，頗有微利，前督臣李率泰、經略洪承疇嘗借帑為之，遂冒昧上疏，未蒙俞允。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Qisheng to reply; Qisheng said: "In the tenth month of Kangxi seventeen when the army advanced to Fenghuang Mountain, because for a time many came to surrender and rewards could not keep pace, I discussed with Governor Wu Xingzuo trade with other provinces, which yielded some small profit; former governor-general Li Shuaitai and Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou had once borrowed treasury funds for this, so I rashly memorialized; it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Qisheng to reply in memorial; Qisheng wrote: "In the tenth month of the seventeenth year of Kangxi, when the army advanced to Fenghuang Mountain, so many came over to our side at once that rewards could not keep pace; I discussed with Governor Wu Xingzuo trade with other provinces, which yielded a modest profit; former governor-general Li Shuaitai and Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou had once borrowed treasury funds for such purposes, so I rashly memorialized—and the request was not granted.

sentences.zh: 臣自入仕，京師未有產業，而軍前捐銀十五萬有奇者，香山罷官後，貿易七年，得積微貲，並臣浙江祖產變價，及親朋借貸，經年累月而後有此。

translations.literal: Since entering office I had no property in the capital, and the more than 150,000 taels donated at the front came from seven years of trade after I was dismissed from Xiangshan, accumulating a small fortune, together with the sale of my ancestral property in Zhejiang and loans from kin and friends, built up year by year before I had this sum.
translations.idiomatic: Since I entered office I have owned no property in the capital; the more than 150,000 taels I donated at the front came from seven years of trade after I was dismissed from Xiangshan, a small sum saved up bit by bit, together with the sale of my ancestral property in Zhejiang and loans from kin and friends—built up over many months and years before I had that amount.

sentences.zh: 臣於十七年七月至省，見總督官廨為耿精忠屯兵毀傷傾圮，因捐貲修整，日役不過數十，柵外員役私舍，令其自行撤除。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventeenth year when I arrived in the province I saw the governor-general's yamen had been occupied and destroyed by Geng Jingzhong's troops and was leaning and ruined; I donated funds to repair it, employing not more than several tens daily; outside the barrier the private quarters of junior officials I had them remove themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventeenth year, when I arrived in the province, I found the governor-general's yamen ruined and leaning after Geng Jingzhong's troops had occupied and wrecked it; I donated funds to repair it, employing no more than several tens of men a day; as for the private quarters of junior officials outside the barrier, I had them tear those down themselves.

sentences.zh: 至臣妾皆有子女，年已老大，並無歌兒舞女，強取戴氏女，尤無其事。

translations.literal: As for my concubines, all have children and are already old; there are no singing girls or dancers; forcibly taking the Dai family's daughter especially has no basis in fact.
translations.idiomatic: As for my concubines, all have borne children and are already advanced in years; I keep no singing girls or dancers; the charge that I forcibly took a daughter of the Dai family is especially without foundation.

sentences.zh: 十八年十一月，臣密陳進剿機宜，請水陸五道進兵，並未阻撓。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighteenth year I secretly memorialized the plan for a punitive expedition, requesting advance by five routes on land and sea, and did not obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eighteenth year I secretly memorialized the plan for a punitive expedition, requesting advance by five routes on land and sea, and I did not obstruct the campaign.

sentences.zh: 至得廈門即攻台灣，先於十八年九月預陳，亦非屆時發議。

translations.literal: As for attacking Taiwan as soon as Xiamen was taken, I had already stated this beforehand in the ninth month of the eighteenth year; it was not a proposal made at the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: As for attacking Taiwan as soon as Xiamen was taken, I had already stated that plan in the ninth month of the eighteenth year; it was not a proposal raised only when the moment arrived.

sentences.zh: 撫臣、提臣拜疏出師，平賊首功已定，臣何所容其慚妒。

translations.literal: When the governor and provincial military commissioner memorialized to take the field and the chief merit for pacifying the rebels was settled, where could I harbor shame and jealousy?
translations.idiomatic: When the governor and provincial military commissioner memorialized to take the field, the chief merit for pacifying the rebels was already settled—where could I harbor shame or jealousy?

sentences.zh: 朱天貴應撫投誠，天貴言之而臣始知之。

translations.literal: Zhu Tiangui was to surrender on the governor's persuasion; Tiangui spoke of it and only then did I learn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tiangui was persuaded to surrender by the governor; Tiangui spoke of it, and only then did I learn of it.

sentences.zh: 臣任三閩三職，雖無妒功之心，實有溺職之咎。

translations.literal: I held three posts in the three Fujian offices; although I have no heart to envy others' merit, I truly bear the guilt of neglecting duty.
translations.idiomatic: I have held three posts across the three Fujian offices; though I have no heart to envy others' merit, I truly bear the guilt of neglecting my duties.

sentences.zh: 乞敕部嚴議，別簡賢能。」

translations.literal: I beg that the ministry deliberate severely and select another able man."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the ministry deliberate on me with severity and choose another able man in my place."

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, report was received.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the court took note.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，敘克海澄、金​​門、廈門功，授世職拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, for merit in taking Haicheng, Jinmen, and Xiamen, he was granted a hereditary office as Butalabuhan combined with Tosalahahan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, for merit in taking Haicheng, Jinmen, and Xiamen, he was granted the hereditary rank of Butalabuhan combined with Tosalahahan.

sentences.zh: 方鄭錦屢入寇，徙濱海居民入內地，俾絕接濟、避侵掠，下令越界者罪至死，民多盪析。

translations.literal: When Zheng Jing repeatedly raided, coastal residents were moved inland to cut off supplies and avoid pillage; those crossing the boundary were sentenced to death, and many families were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: While Zheng Jing raided again and again, coastal inhabitants were moved inland to cut off supplies to the enemy and avoid pillage; anyone crossing the boundary was sentenced to death, and countless families were scattered.

sentences.zh: 及禁旅班師，驅系良民子女北行，啟聖白王嚴禁。

translations.literal: When the prohibition troops were withdrawn, they drove good commoners' sons and daughters northward; Qisheng informed the prince and strictly forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: When the prohibition troops were withdrawn, they drove the sons and daughters of good commoners northward; Qisheng reported this to the prince and had it strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 复捐貲贖歸難民二萬餘人，並請開海界、复民業，聽降卒墾荒，民困漸蘇。

translations.literal: He again donated funds to redeem more than twenty thousand refugees and requested opening the maritime boundary and restoring people's livelihoods, allowing surrendered soldiers to open wasteland, and the people's hardship gradually eased.
translations.idiomatic: He again donated funds to ransom more than twenty thousand refugees, and requested that the maritime boundary be opened and people's livelihoods restored, allowing surrendered soldiers to reclaim wasteland; the people's hardship gradually eased.

sentences.zh: 及錦死，子克塽仍其爵，稱延平王，凡事皆決之國軒等。

translations.literal: When Jing died, his son Keshuang inherited the title, styled himself Prince Yanping, and all affairs were decided by Guoxuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Jing died, his son Keshuang inherited his rank, styled himself Prince Yanping, and all affairs were decided by Guoxuan and his circle.

sentences.zh: 啟聖令知府卞永譽、張仲舉專理海疆，多以金帛間其黨與。

translations.literal: Qisheng ordered prefects Bian Yongyu and Zhang Zhongju to manage the coast exclusively, and often used gold and silk to sow discord among their factions.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng put prefects Bian Yongyu and Zhang Zhongju in charge of the coast and often used gold and silk to sow discord among the enemy factions.

sentences.zh: 克塽乃遣使齎書，原稱臣入貢，不薙發登岸，如琉球、高麗例。

translations.literal: Keshuang then sent envoys with a letter, offering to submit as a vassal and pay tribute without shaving the head when landing on shore, as in the cases of Ryukyu and Koryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Keshuang then sent envoys bearing a letter, offering to submit as a vassal and pay tribute without shaving the head when coming ashore, on the model of Ryukyu and Koryeo.

sentences.zh: 啟聖以聞，上不許，趣水師提督施琅進徵。

translations.literal: Qisheng reported this; the emperor did not permit it and urged naval commander Shi Lang to advance in expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng reported this to the throne; the emperor would not agree and urged the naval commander Shi Lang to advance in expedition.

sentences.zh: 二十二年六月，瑯進攻台灣，取澎湖。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Lang advanced on Taiwan and took Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Shi Lang advanced on Taiwan and took Penghu.

sentences.zh: 啟聖駐廈門督饋運，以大舟載金、纟曾、貨、米至軍，大賚降卒，遣之歸，台民果攜貳。

translations.literal: Qisheng was stationed at Xiamen supervising supplies; he loaded large ships with gold, silk, goods, and rice to the army, richly rewarded the surrendered soldiers, and sent them home; the people of Taiwan indeed became divided in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng was stationed at Xiamen supervising supply transport; he sent large ships laden with gold, silk, goods, and rice to the army, richly rewarded the surrendered troops, and sent them home—and the people of Taiwan did indeed waver in their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 復設間使克塽與國軒互相猜，眾莫為用。

translations.literal: He again set secret agents to make Keshuang and Guoxuan suspect each other so that none could be employed effectively.
translations.idiomatic: He again set secret agents to sow mutual suspicion between Keshuang and Guoxuan, so that no one could be put to effective use.

sentences.zh: 瑯遂定台灣，克塽、國軒等皆降。

translations.literal: Lang then pacified Taiwan; Keshuang, Guoxuan, and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lang then pacified Taiwan; Keshuang, Guoxuan, and the rest all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 語具瑯傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in full in Lang's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in Shi Lang's biography.

sentences.zh: 啟聖還福州，未幾，疽發背，卒。

translations.literal: Qisheng returned to Fuzhou; before long a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng returned to Fuzhou; before long a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.

sentences.zh: 明年，部議以啟聖修繕船舶、軍械，浮冒帑金四萬七千有奇，應追繳，上念其勞，免之。

translations.literal: The next year the ministry deliberated that Qisheng in repairing ships and military equipment had falsely claimed more than forty-seven thousand taels of treasury funds and it should be recovered; the emperor mindful of his labors exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the ministry ruled that in repairing ships and military equipment Qisheng had falsely claimed more than forty-seven thousand taels of treasury funds, which ought to be recovered; the emperor, mindful of his services, exempted him.

sentences.zh: 子儀，膂力絕人，雄偉與父埒。

translations.literal: His son Yi had extraordinary physical strength and was as imposing as his father.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi had strength beyond ordinary men and was as imposing as his father.

sentences.zh: 初以捐納知縣從征，累戰有功。

translations.literal: At first by purchase he became a magistrate and followed the expedition, repeatedly distinguishing himself in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At first, having purchased office as a magistrate, he joined the campaign and distinguished himself again and again in battle.

sentences.zh: 康親王檄署游擊。

translations.literal: Prince Kang's order appointed him acting colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang appointed him acting colonel by order.

sentences.zh: 議敘，內擢郎中。

translations.literal: When merit was discussed he was promoted within the ranks to director in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was reckoned he was promoted within the civil service to director in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 上以儀有才略，且自陳原以武職自效，改都督僉事，以總兵用。

translations.literal: The emperor because Yi had talent and strategy, and he himself had stated he wished to serve in a military post, changed him to vice commissioner of the metropolitan banner, and employed him as regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing that Yi had talent and strategy and that he himself had declared he wished to serve in a military post, changed his appointment to vice commissioner of the metropolitan banner and employed him as a regional commander.

sentences.zh: 歷狼山、杭州、沅州、鶴慶諸鎮總兵，鑲紅旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: He served successively as regional commander of Langshan, Hangzhou, Yuanzhou, and Heqing, and as vice commandant-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner Hanjun.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as regional commander at Langshan, Hangzhou, Yuanzhou, and Heqing, and as vice commandant-in-chief of the Han Bannermen of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: He died; imperial sacrifices and funeral were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and the court granted him the rites of imperial sacrifice and burial.

sentences.zh: 鍾寶，少業屠，流為盜。

translations.literal: Zhong Bao in youth worked as a butcher and drifted into banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Bao had been a butcher in his youth and drifted into banditry.

sentences.zh: 啟聖令香山，招之降。

translations.literal: When Qisheng was magistrate of Xiangshan he recruited him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Qisheng was magistrate of Xiangshan he induced him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 後啟聖徵福建，寶偕同降者二十人隸麾下，每戰輒當前，所向有功。

translations.literal: Later when Qisheng campaigned in Fujian, Bao with twenty others who surrendered together joined his command; in each battle he took the front and wherever he went had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Qisheng campaigned in Fujian, Bao and twenty others who had surrendered with him entered his service; in every battle he took the front rank and wherever he went won distinction.

sentences.zh: 累進秩都督僉事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice commissioner of the metropolitan banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted until he reached the rank of vice commissioner of the metropolitan banner.

sentences.zh: 啟聖卒，遂歸。

translations.literal: When Qisheng died he then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Qisheng died he went home.

sentences.zh: 後數年，部議注官，授潼關參將，遷靖邊協副將。

translations.literal: Several years later, when the ministry deliberated on registering officials, he was appointed defender of Tong Pass and transferred to assistant regional commander of Jingbian.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, when the ministry deliberated on registering officials, he was appointed defender of Tong Pass and later transferred to assistant regional commander of the Jingbian command.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 寶撫兵民有恩，稱為鍾佛子。

translations.literal: Bao treated soldiers and commoners with kindness and was called the Buddha-son Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Bao treated soldiers and commoners with kindness and was called the Buddha-son Zhong.

sentences.zh: 韓大任，降後入覲，聖祖以其為三桂將，留為內務府包衣參領。

translations.literal: Han Daren, after surrendering, had an audience; the Sacred Ancestor because he had been Wu Sangui's general kept him as a bondservant clerk in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren, after surrendering, had an audience with the emperor; because he had been a general under Wu Sangui, the Kangxi Emperor kept him on as a bondservant clerk in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，從佟國綱徵噶爾丹，次烏闌布通，伏發，國綱歿於陣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he followed Tong Guogang in the expedition against Galdan; they encamped at Ulan Butong; an ambush was sprung and Guogang died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he followed Tong Guogang on the expedition against Galdan; they encamped at Ulan Butong; an ambush was sprung and Guogang fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 大任驚曰：「吾聞臨陣失帥，兵家大罪。

translations.literal: Daren cried out in alarm: "I have heard that losing the commander in battle is a grave military offense.
translations.idiomatic: Daren cried out in alarm: "I have heard that to lose one's commander in battle is a grave offense in the art of war.

sentences.zh: 吾以叛逆之黨，蒙恩不死。

translations.literal: I am of the rebellious faction and received grace not to be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: I belong to the party of rebels and received grace that I was not put to death.

sentences.zh: 今豈可坐必死之律，復對獄吏乎？」

translations.literal: Now how can I sit under the law that must mean death and again face prison officers?"
translations.idiomatic: How can I now sit under a law that must mean death and face the prison officers again?"

sentences.zh: 因馳入賊陣，手刃數十人，死之。

translations.literal: So he galloped into the enemy formation, killed several tens with his own hand, and died.
translations.idiomatic: With that he galloped into the enemy ranks, killed several tens with his own hand, and died.

sentences.zh: 吳興祚，字伯成，漢軍正紅旗人，原籍浙江山陰。

translations.literal: Wu Xingzuo, courtesy name Bocheng, was a Hanjun of the Plain Red Banner, originally from Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingzuo, whose courtesy name was Bocheng, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Red Banner, originally from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父執忠，客禮親王代善幕，授頭等護衛。

translations.literal: His father Zhizhong, as a guest at Prince Dai Shan's staff, was appointed a first-class guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhizhong, received as a guest at Prince Dai Shan's staff, was appointed a first-class guard.

sentences.zh: 興祚自貢生授江西萍鄉知縣。

translations.literal: Xingzuo from purchase as a student was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo, having purchased office as a student, was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓叛，郡縣多被寇，萍鄉以有備獨完。

translations.literal: When Jin Shengchuan rebelled, prefectures and counties were largely overrun by bandits; Pingxiang alone remained intact because it was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Shengchuan rebelled, bandits overran most of the prefectures and counties, but Pingxiang alone remained intact because it had been prepared.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 旋以守禦功复官，授山西大寧知縣，遷山東沂州知州。

translations.literal: Soon, on merit in defense, he was restored to office; he was appointed magistrate of Daying in Shanxi, then transferred to be prefect of Yizhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to office for his defensive merit, appointed magistrate of Daying in Shanxi, and then transferred to prefect of Yizhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 白蓮教嘯聚為患，興祚開諭散遣之。

translations.literal: The White Lotus sect gathered and clamored, becoming a calamity; Xingzuo openly admonished them and dispersed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the White Lotus sect gathered in armed bands and became a menace, Xingzuo openly reasoned with them and had them disbanded.

sentences.zh: 复坐事降補江南無錫知縣。

translations.literal: Again on account of an offense he was demoted and transferred to serve as magistrate of Wuxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was again demoted for misconduct and reassigned as magistrate of Wuxi in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 縣吏虧庫帑，更數政未得償，官罷不能去。

translations.literal: County clerks had embezzled the treasury; through several administrations the loss could not be repaid; when an official was dismissed he could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: County clerks had embezzled public funds, and through several administrations the shortfall could never be made up—when an official was dismissed he still could not leave.

sentences.zh: 興祚至，為請豁除，其當償者出私財代輸。

translations.literal: When Xingzuo arrived, he requested remission; what still had to be repaid he paid from private funds on others' behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzuo arrived, he petitioned for remission of the debt, and for what still had to be repaid he paid out of his own purse.

sentences.zh: 清丈通縣田，編號繪圖，因田徵賦。

translations.literal: He clearly surveyed all the county fields, assigned numbers and drew maps, and levied taxes according to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted a full survey of the county's fields, numbered them and mapped them, and levied taxes according to actual holdings.

sentences.zh: 飛詭隱匿，皆不得行。

translations.literal: False reporting and concealment could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: False claims and concealment could no longer be practiced.

sentences.zh: 縣徭役未均，最煩苦者為圖六。

translations.literal: Corvee labor in the county was uneven; the most burdensome was for Register Six.
translations.idiomatic: Corvee duties in the county were unevenly distributed, and the worst burden fell on Register Six.

sentences.zh: 興祚以入官田徵租僱役，民害乃除。

translations.literal: Xingzuo used income from government fields to levy rent and hire labor for corvee; the people's harm was then removed.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo used rents from government land to hire corvee labor, and the people's burden was lifted.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，為粥食餓者。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, he made gruel to feed the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he set up gruel kitchens to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 八旗兵駐防蘇州，興祚請於領兵固山，單騎彈壓。

translations.literal: Eight Banner troops were garrisoned at Suzhou; Xingzuo requested of the gushan leading the troops and alone on horseback suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Eight Banner troops were garrisoned at Suzhou, Xingzuo obtained permission from their garrison commander and rode out alone to enforce order.

sentences.zh: 兵或取民雞，立笞之，皆奉約束。

translations.literal: If soldiers took the people's chickens, he immediately had them beaten; all obeyed discipline.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers seized people's chickens he had them flogged on the spot, and they all submitted to discipline.

sentences.zh: 塘溢，兵不得渡，立竹於塘旁，懸燈以為識，騎行如坦途。

translations.literal: A pond overflowed, and soldiers could not cross; he set up bamboo poles beside the pond and hung lamps as markers, and riding was like on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: When a pond overflowed and blocked the soldiers' crossing, he planted bamboo poles along the bank and hung lanterns as markers, so that riding across was as easy as traveling a level road.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，遷行人，仍留知縣事，用漕運總督帥顏保薦，超擢福建按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he was transferred to Gentleman Attendant, yet still retained magistrate duties; on recommendation of Grand Canal transport commissioner Shuai Yanbao he was exceptionally promoted to Fujian surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he was transferred to Gentleman Attendant while still handling magistrate duties, and on the recommendation of Grand Canal transport commissioner Shuai Yanbao he was promoted out of turn to surveillance commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 有朱統錩者，號明裔，耿精忠私署敉遠將軍，及精忠降，自稱宜春王，據貴溪為亂，與福建錯壤。

translations.literal: There was one Zhu Tongqi, who styled himself a Ming descendant; Geng Jingzhong had privately appointed him Pacification-General of the Frontier, and when Jingzhong surrendered, he styled himself Prince of Yichun, seized Guixi and raised rebellion, bordering Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhu Tongqi styled himself a descendant of the Ming; Geng Jingzhong had privately appointed him Pacification-General of the Frontier, and after Jingzhong surrendered he proclaimed himself Prince of Yichun, seized Guixi, and rebelled on Fujian's border.

sentences.zh: 興祚輕騎至光澤，撫其將陳龍等，遣降將陽自歸為內應，令龍導師入，其將馮珩等縛統錩，率兵三千以降。

translations.literal: Xingzuo with a light escort went to Guangze, pacified his generals Chen Long and others, sent the surrendering general Yang Zigui as an inside contact, ordered Long to guide the army in; his generals Feng Heng and others bound Tongqi and led three thousand troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo rode lightly to Guangze and won over Zhu's generals Chen Long and others; he sent the surrendered general Yang Zigui as an inside agent, had Long guide the imperial army in, and Feng Heng and others bound Zhu Tongqi and surrendered with three thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 時鄭錦踞台灣，遣其驍將劉國軒等陷漳、泉屬縣，复圍泉州。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Jing held Taiwan; he sent his fierce generals Liu Guoxuan and others to seize counties under Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, and again besieged Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing then held Taiwan and sent his best generals, including Liu Guoxuan, to seize counties under Zhangzhou and Quanzhou and once again besiege Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 興祚率標兵自興化赴援，至仙遊，錦將黃球等率二千人結土寇萬餘屯白鴿嶺。

translations.literal: Xingzuo led garrison troops from Xinghua to the relief; reaching Xianyou, Jing's generals Huang Qiu and others led two thousand men, joining more than ten thousand local bandits, and encamped at Baige Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo led garrison troops from Xinghua to the rescue, and at Xianyou Zheng Jing's generals Huang Qiu and others, with two thousand men joined by more than ten thousand local bandits, encamped at Baige Ridge.

sentences.zh: 興祚分兵三道，自當中路，與戰，自辰至酉，相持不即退。

translations.literal: Xingzuo divided his force into three columns, himself taking the center; they fought from the chen hour to the you hour, locked in stalemate without immediate retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo divided his forces into three columns and took the center himself; the battle raged from morning until evening without either side yielding ground.

sentences.zh: 興祚遣兵自間道奪白鴿嶺關口，斬級六百，墮岸溺水死者甚眾，寇乃潰走，追敗之於嶺頭灣，复永春、德化二縣。

translations.literal: Xingzuo sent troops by a hidden path to seize Baige Ridge pass; six hundred heads were taken, many fell from cliffs and drowned; the bandits then fled in rout; pursuing he defeated them at Lingtou Bay and recovered Yongchun and Dehua counties.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo sent troops by a side path to seize the pass at Baige Ridge, took six hundred heads, and many rebels fell from the cliffs and drowned; the enemy then broke and fled, and he pursued and routed them at Lingtou Bay, recovering Yongchun and Dehua.

sentences.zh: 國軒自泉州走入海，以巨艦數百出沒赤嶼、黃崎諸處。

translations.literal: Guoxuan from Quanzhou fled to the sea, and with several hundred large ships appeared and vanished at Chiyu, Huangqi, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan fled from Quanzhou out to sea and with several hundred large warships raided around Chiyu, Huangqi, and other points along the coast.

sentences.zh: 興祚遣總兵林賢等統水師出海，分三路夾攻，焚敵艦六十餘，俘斬六千有奇。

translations.literal: Xingzuo sent regional commander Lin Xian and others to lead the naval force out to sea, attacking in three columns; more than sixty enemy ships were burned, more than six thousand captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo sent regional commander Lin Xian and others to lead the fleet to sea, attacked in three columns, burned more than sixty enemy ships, and captured or killed more than six thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 疏報捷，並言：「海逆逼犯漳、泉，大軍由陸路進發，跋涉疲難。

translations.literal: In a memorial he reported victory, and also stated: "The sea rebels press upon and invade Zhang and Quan; the great army advances by land routes, toiling and weary with hardship.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized reporting victory and added: "The sea rebels are pressing in on Zhangzhou and Quanzhou; the main army advances overland, exhausted by the long march.

sentences.zh: 臣前捐募水兵，一戰破賊，但兵力稍薄，未易輕取廈門。

translations.literal: Your subject previously contributed to recruit naval troops, and in one battle broke the bandits, but the troops are somewhat thin, not easy lightly to take Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject previously raised naval troops at his own expense and defeated the rebels in one battle, but our forces are still too thin to take Xiamen easily.

sentences.zh: 若得水師二萬，再添造戰船，可直搗巢穴，掃蕩鯨波。」

translations.literal: If one obtains twenty thousand naval troops, and further builds battle ships, one can directly strike the nest, and sweep the whale waves."
translations.idiomatic: With twenty thousand naval troops and more warships, we could strike their stronghold directly and sweep the seas clean.

sentences.zh: 詔允行。

translations.literal: The edict approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 十八年，國軒率兵二千至郭塘、歐溪頭，欲斷江東橋以犯長泰，興祚與都統吉勒塔布、總督姚啟聖會師擊走之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan led two thousand troops to Guotang and Ouxitou, intending to cut Jiangdong Bridge to invade Changtai; Xingzuo joined commandant-in-chief Jiletabu and governor Yao Qisheng, united armies and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Liu Guoxuan led two thousand men to Guotang and Ouxitou, intending to sever Jiangdong Bridge and invade Changtai; Xingzuo joined commandant-in-chief Jiletabu and Governor Yao Qisheng, and together they drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 興祚遣驛傳道王國泰等招降錦將蔡衝琱、林忠等三百八十五人，兵萬二千五百，拔難民千二百，得舟六十七。

translations.literal: Xingzuo sent courier Wang Guotai and others to induce surrender of Jing's generals Cai Chongdiao, Lin Zhong, and three hundred eighty-five others, troops twelve thousand five hundred, rescued one thousand two hundred refugees, and obtained sixty-seven boats.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo dispatched Wang Guotai and others via the courier service to win over Zheng Jing's generals Cai Chongdiao, Lin Zhong, and 385 others along with 12,500 troops; they rescued 1,200 refugees and seized sixty-seven boats.

sentences.zh: 敘前後功，進秩正一品。

translations.literal: Recording his former and later merits, he was advanced in rank to first grade.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his successive victories he was promoted to the first rank.

sentences.zh: 十九年，疏言：「鄭錦盤踞廈門，沿海生靈受其荼毒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he memorialized, stating: "Zheng Jing occupies Xiamen; the people along the coast suffer his torment.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he memorialized: "Zheng Jing holds Xiamen, and the coastal population suffers under his oppression.

sentences.zh: 臣去冬新造戰船，水師提督萬正色分配將士，自閩安出大洋操練。

translations.literal: Your subject last winter newly built battle ships; naval commissioner Wan Zhengse assigned officers and troops; from Min'an they went out to the open sea for drill.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter your subject had new warships built, and naval commissioner Wan Zhengse assigned officers and men to train on the open sea from Min'an.

sentences.zh: 俟舊存船艘修葺完整，江南砲手齊集，即相機進取廈門。」

translations.literal: When the existing ships are repaired whole, and Jiangnan gunners are all assembled, then as opportunity offers advance and take Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Once the remaining vessels are fully repaired and the Jiangnan gunners are assembled, we shall seize the opportunity to take Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 二月，正色師進海壇，興祚自泉州會寧海將軍拉哈達、總兵王英等赴同安，攻克汭洲、潯尾諸隘。

translations.literal: In the second month Zhengse's army advanced to Haitan; Xingzuo from Quanzhou joined Ninghai general Lahada, regional commander Wang Ying, and others, went to Tong'an, and stormed Ruizhou, Xunwei, and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wan Zhengse's fleet advanced on Haitan, while Xingzuo left Quanzhou to join Ninghai general Lahada and regional commander Wang Ying at Tong'an, where they stormed the passes at Ruizhou, Xunwei, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 渡海，拉哈達出中路，英右，興祚左，奮戰，敵大潰，遂克廈門。

translations.literal: Crossing the sea, Lahada took the center route, Ying the right, Xingzuo the left; they fought fiercely; the enemy greatly routed; then Xiamen was taken.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the sea with Lahada in the center, Wang Ying on the right, and Xingzuo on the left; after fierce fighting the enemy broke completely, and Xiamen fell.

sentences.zh: 時正色已取海壇，降錦將朱天貴等，復遣兵取金門，餘眾悉竄台灣。

translations.literal: At that time Zhengse had already taken Haitan, induced Jing's generals Zhu Tiangui and others to surrender; again sent troops to take Jinmen; the remaining masses all fled to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wan Zhengse had already taken Haitan and won the surrender of Zheng Jing's generals Zhu Tiangui and others; he sent troops again to take Jinmen, and the rest of the enemy fled to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉獎，下部優敘。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, an edict praised and rewarded; orders were sent down for superior merit evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, the emperor issued an edict of commendation and ordered exceptional rewards for the officers involved.

sentences.zh: 興祚因請留澳民防守，蠲荒田租糧，減關課。

translations.literal: Xingzuo thereupon requested to keep Ao residents for defense, remit grain tax on wasteland fields, and reduce customs levies.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo also petitioned to keep local harbor communities on guard duty, to remit grain tax on abandoned fields, and to reduce customs duties.

sentences.zh: 正色亦請於海澄、廈門分兵駐守。

translations.literal: Zhengse also requested to divide troops and garrison at Haicheng and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Zhengse likewise requested that troops be stationed at Haicheng and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 上命侍郎溫岱赴福建會議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered vice president Wen Dai to go to Fujian for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent vice minister Wen Dai to Fujian to confer on the matter.

sentences.zh: 溫岱至，啟聖與言正色复海壇，與天貴先有約乃進兵，無殺賊攻克事。

translations.literal: When Wen Dai arrived, Qisheng told him that when Zhengse recovered Haitan, he had a prior agreement with Tian Gui before advancing troops; there was no matter of killing bandits to capture by storm.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Dai arrived, Yao Qisheng told him that Wan Zhengse had retaken Haitan only after making a prior deal with Zhu Tian Gui, and that no enemy had been killed in its capture.

sentences.zh: 溫岱還京師，兵部據其言，議興祚冒功，上命仍議敘，予世職拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Wen Dai returned to the capital; the Board of War based on his words debated that Xingzuo falsely claimed merit; the emperor ordered merit still be evaluated; granted hereditary office as Butalabuhan combined with Tosalahahan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Dai returned to the capital, the Board of War, acting on his report, considered that Xingzuo had falsely claimed credit, but the emperor ordered that merit be evaluated nonetheless and granted him the hereditary rank of Butalabuhan combined with Tosalahahan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to governor-general of the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 興祚上官，疏言尚之信在廣東橫徵苛斂，民受其害數十年。

translations.literal: When Xingzuo assumed his post, he memorialized that Shang Zhixin in Guangdong had levied harshly and extortionately; the people had suffered for decades.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Xingzuo memorialized that Shang Zhixin had been levying extortionate taxes in Guangdong, and that the people had suffered under this for decades.

sentences.zh: 因舉鹽埠、渡稅、稅總店、漁課諸害，悉奏罷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cited the abuses of salt wharves, ferry taxes, tax general shops, and fishing levies, and memorialized to abolish them all.
translations.idiomatic: He cited abuses such as the salt wharves, ferry taxes, tax monopolies, and fishing levies, and had them all abolished by imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 自遷界令下，廣東沿海居民多失業，興祚疏請展界，恣民捕採耕種。

translations.literal: Since the coastal evacuation order was issued, many Guangdong coastal residents lost livelihood; Xingzuo memorialized requesting boundary extension, allowing the people freely to fish, gather, and cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: Since the coastal evacuation order, many residents along the Guangdong coast had lost their livelihoods; Xingzuo memorialized asking that the boundary be extended so people could again fish, forage, and farm freely.

sentences.zh: 上遣尚書杜臻、內閣學士石柱會興祚巡歷規畫，兵民皆得所。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched ministers Du Zhen and Grand Secretariat academician Shizhu to join Xingzuo in touring and planning; troops and civilians all found their place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Minister Du Zhen and Grand Secretariat academician Shizhu to join Xingzuo in surveying and planning the resettlement, so that both soldiers and civilians were properly settled.

sentences.zh: 又言潮州海汛遼闊，商民往來貿易，恐宵小潛踪，應令澄海協達濠營水汛官兵船隻改歸南澳水師鎮統轄，與碣石鎮互相聯絡，巡防外海島嶼，詔並允行。

translations.literal: He also stated that the Chaozhou coastal patrol was vast; merchants coming and going to trade—fearing petty men lurking—should order Chenghai brigade Dahao camp naval patrol officers, soldiers, and vessels to be changed and placed under Nanao naval commandant's jurisdiction, with Jieshi garrison mutually linking, patrolling outer sea islands; the edict approved all.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the Chaozhou coastal zone was too vast for merchants traveling to and fro, and that covert troublemakers might go unnoticed; he proposed placing the Chenghai brigade's Dahao naval patrol force under the Nanao naval command, coordinating with the Jieshi garrison to patrol the outer islands—and the emperor approved all of these measures.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，疏請於廣東、廣西二省設爐鼓鑄，給事中錢晉錫、御史王君詔疏劾興祚鼓鑄浮冒，下吏議，當鐫秩，命以副都統用。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year, memorialized requesting in Guangdong and Guangxi two provinces to establish furnace minting; supervising secretary Qian Jinxi and censor Wang Junzhao memorialized impeaching Xingzuo for inflated minting; referred to officials for deliberation, should be stripped of rank; ordered to serve as deputy lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, he memorialized asking that mints be established in Guangdong and Guangxi. The supervising secretary Qian Jinxi and the censor Wang Junzhao then impeached Xingzuo for fraudulent minting. The case was sent down for official review, and he was judged liable to be stripped of rank; yet he was ordered to serve as a deputy lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，授歸化城右翼漢軍副都統，复坐事鐫秩。

translations.literal: Thirty-first year, appointed deputy lieutenant general of the Right Wing Han Army at Guihua City; again for an offense stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was appointed deputy lieutenant general of the Right Wing Han Army at Guihua City, but was again stripped of rank after an offense.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上徵噶爾丹，命自呼坦和碩至寧夏安十三塘，興祚原效力坐沙克舒爾塘，未幾，復原秩。

translations.literal: Thirty-fifth year, the Emperor campaigned against Galdan, ordered from Hutai Heshuo to Ningxia An's thirteen stations; Xingzuo originally volunteered to serve, stationed at Shakushu'er station; before long, restored to original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year the Emperor marched against Galdan and ordered supply stations established from Hutai Heshuo to the thirteen stations at Ningxia An. Xingzuo volunteered for duty and was posted at Shakushu'er station; before long his original rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，卒。

translations.literal: Thirty-sixth year, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 興祚為政持大體，除煩苛，卒後遠近戴之。

translations.literal: Xingzuo in governing held to the broad principles, removed troublesome exactions; after death near and far revered him.
translations.idiomatic: In office Xingzuo kept to the larger principles of governance and cleared away petty burdens; after his death people near and far honored his memory.

sentences.zh: 歷官之地，並籥祀名宦。

translations.literal: Places where he served as official, all entered the rooster-sign memorial rolls for distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: Every place where he had served entered him into the rolls of the local shrines to distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 施琅，字琢公，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: Shi Lang, styled Zhuogong, a native of Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lang, courtesy name Zhuogong, was a native of Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 初為明總兵鄭芝龍部下左衝鋒。

translations.literal: Initially served as left vanguard under Ming regional commander Zheng Zhilong.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as a left vanguard under the Ming regional commander Zheng Zhilong.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，師定福建，瑯從芝龍降。

translations.literal: Shunzhi third year, the army pacified Fujian; Lang followed Zhilong in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, when imperial forces pacified Fujian, Lang surrendered along with Zhilong.

sentences.zh: 從征廣東，戡定順德、東莞、三水、新寧諸縣。

translations.literal: Followed the campaign in Guangdong, pacified Shunde, Dongguan, Sanshui, Xinning and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign in Guangdong and helped pacify Shunde, Dongguan, Sanshui, Xinning, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 芝龍歸京師，其子成功竄踞海島，招瑯，不從。

translations.literal: Zhilong returned to the capital; his son Chenggong fled and occupied an island, summoned Lang; Lang did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhilong went to the capital, his son Chenggong fled to an island and seized it, then summoned Lang to join him; Lang refused.

sentences.zh: 成功執瑯，並縶其家屬。

translations.literal: Chenggong seized Lang and also imprisoned his family members.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong seized Lang and imprisoned his entire family as well.

sentences.zh: 瑯以計得脫，父大宣、弟顯及子侄皆為成功所殺。

translations.literal: Lang by a stratagem escaped; his father Da Xuan, brother Xian, and sons and nephews were all killed by Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: Lang escaped by a ruse, but his father Da Xuan, his brother Xian, and his sons and nephews were all killed by Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從定遠大將軍世子濟度擊敗成功於福州，授同安副將。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, followed the Campaign General of Dingyuan, the Heir Jidu, in defeating Chenggong at Fuzhou; appointed deputy commander of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he followed the Campaign General of Dingyuan, the Heir Jidu, in defeating Chenggong at Fuzhou and was appointed deputy commander of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 十六年，成功據台灣，就擢瑯同安總兵。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, Chenggong occupied Taiwan; thereupon Lang was promoted to commander of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, after Chenggong seized Taiwan, Lang was promoted to commander of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，遷水師提督。

translations.literal: Kangxi first year, transferred to naval commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he was transferred to the post of naval commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時成功已死，其子錦率眾欲犯海澄，瑯遣守備汪明等率舟師御之海門，斬其將林維，獲戰船、軍械。

translations.literal: At the time Chenggong had already died; his son Jing led troops intending to attack Haicheng; Lang sent garrison commander Wang Ming and others to lead the fleet to defend at Haimen, beheaded their general Lin Wei, and captured warships and military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chenggong was dead, and his son Jing led a force intending to strike Haicheng. Lang sent the garrison commander Wang Ming and others with a fleet to meet them at Haimen, killed their general Lin Wei, and captured warships and arms.

sentences.zh: 未幾，靖南王耿繼茂、總督李率泰等攻克廈門，敵驚潰，瑯募荷蘭國水兵，以夾板船要擊，斬級千餘，乘勝取浯嶼、金門二島。

translations.literal: Before long, Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao, Governor Li Shuaitai and others captured Xiamen; the enemy fled in panic; Lang recruited Dutch naval troops and used frigate ships to intercept and attack, beheaded over a thousand, and taking advantage of victory seized the two islands of Wuyu and Jinmen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao, Governor Li Shuaitai, and others captured Xiamen, and the enemy broke in panic. Lang hired Dutch sailors and used frigates to cut them off, killing more than a thousand men, then pressed the advantage to take the islands of Wuyu and Jinmen.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加右都督。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded; he was given the additional rank of Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recognized, and he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三年，加靖海將軍。

translations.literal: Third year, given the additional title Pacifying-the-Seas General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was given the additional title of Pacifying-the-Seas General.

sentences.zh: 七年，瑯密陳錦負嵎海上，宜急攻之。

translations.literal: Seventh year, Lang secretly memorialized that Jing was clinging defiantly on the sea and should be attacked urgently.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Lang secretly memorialized that Jing was defying the court from the sea and ought to be attacked at once.

sentences.zh: 召詣京師，上詢方略，瑯言：「賊兵不滿數万，戰船不過數百，錦智勇俱無。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital; the Emperor inquired about strategy. Lang said: "The rebels' troops are fewer than ten thousand, and their warships no more than several hundred; Jing has neither wisdom nor courage.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital, and when the Emperor asked his plan Lang replied: "The rebels have fewer than ten thousand men and no more than a few hundred warships; Jing lacks both wit and valor.

sentences.zh: 若先取澎湖以扼其吭，賊勢立絀；

translations.literal: If we first take Penghu to choke their throat, the rebels' strength will immediately fail;
translations.idiomatic: If we first seize Penghu and cut off their lifeline, the rebels' strength will collapse at once;

sentences.zh: 倘复負固，則重師泊台灣港口，而別以奇兵分襲南路打狗港及北路文​​港海翁堀。

translations.literal: If they again hold firm, then a main force should moor at Taiwan's harbor, while separately surprise troops divide to attack the southern route at Takao and the northern route at Wengang and Haiwengju.
translations.idiomatic: If they still resist, a main fleet should anchor off Taiwan's ports while separate strike forces hit the southern route at Takao and the northern route at Wengang and Haiwengju.

sentences.zh: 賊分則力薄，合則勢蹙，台灣計日可平。」

translations.literal: If the rebels divide, their strength is thin; if they unite, their situation is tight; Taiwan can be pacified within days."
translations.idiomatic: Divided, the rebels will be too weak; united, they will be cornered; Taiwan can be pacified within days."

sentences.zh: 事下部議，寢其奏。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation, and his memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was sent to the ministries for review, and his memorial was set aside.

sentences.zh: 因裁水師提督，授瑯內大臣，隸鑲黃旗漢軍。

translations.literal: Because the naval commander-in-chief post was abolished, Lang was appointed an inner court minister and attached to the Bordered Yellow Banner Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: The naval command was then abolished, and Lang was made an inner court minister attached to the Bordered Yellow Banner Han Army.

sentences.zh: 二十年，錦死，子克塽幼，諸將劉國軒、馮錫範用事。

translations.literal: Twentieth year, Jing died; his son Ke Shuang was young; the generals Liu Guoxuan and Feng Xifan held power.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Jing died, leaving his young son Ke Shuang; the generals Liu Guoxuan and Feng Xifan then held the reins of power.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士李光地奏台灣可取狀，因薦​​瑯習海上事，上复授瑯福建水師提督，加太子少保，諭相機進取。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Guangdi memorialized that Taiwan could be taken and recommended Lang as skilled in maritime affairs; the Emperor again appointed Lang Fujian naval commander-in-chief, added Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince, and instructed him to advance when the moment was right.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Guangdi memorialized that Taiwan could be taken and recommended Lang for his mastery of maritime affairs. The Emperor restored him as Fujian naval commander-in-chief, made him Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince, and ordered him to strike when conditions favored it.

sentences.zh: 瑯至軍，疏言：「賊船久泊澎湖，悉力固守。

translations.literal: Lang arrived at the army and memorialized: "The rebel ships have long been moored at Penghu, exerting all their strength in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang reached the fleet he memorialized: "The rebel ships have long been anchored at Penghu and are defending it with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 冬春之際，颶風時發，我舟驟難過洋。

translations.literal: Between winter and spring, hurricanes often arise; our ships suddenly find it hard to cross the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Between winter and spring hurricanes often blow up, and our ships cannot easily make the crossing.

sentences.zh: 臣今練習水師，又遣間諜通臣舊時部曲，使為內應。

translations.literal: Your servant is now drilling the navy and also sending spies to contact my former subordinates, so that they may serve as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: I am now training the fleet and sending agents to my former subordinates to arrange inside support.

sentences.zh: 俟風便，可獲全勝。」

translations.literal: Awaiting favorable wind, we can obtain complete victory."
translations.idiomatic: When the wind turns favorable, we can win a complete victory."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，給事中孫蕙疏言宜緩徵台灣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the supervising secretary Sun Hui memorialized that the Taiwan campaign should be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the supervising secretary Sun Hui memorialized that the expedition against Taiwan should be postponed.

sentences.zh: 七月，彗星見，戶部尚書梁清標復以為言，詔暫緩進剿。

translations.literal: In the seventh month a comet appeared; Minister of Revenue Liang Qingbiao again spoke on this; an edict temporarily delayed the punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month a comet appeared, and Minister of Revenue Liang Qingbiao raised the matter again; an edict then temporarily halted the advance.

sentences.zh: 瑯疏言：「臣已簡水師精兵二萬、戰船三百，足破滅海賊。

translations.literal: Lang memorialized: "Your servant has already selected twenty thousand elite naval troops and three hundred warships, sufficient to destroy and extinguish the sea rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Lang memorialized: "I have already chosen twenty thousand picked sailors and three hundred warships, enough to destroy the sea rebels.

sentences.zh: 請趣督撫治糧餉，但遇風利，即可進行，並請調陸路官兵協剿。」

translations.literal: I request that the governors and grand coordinators be urgently urged to prepare grain and pay; whenever the wind is favorable, we can immediately advance, and I also request that land-route officers and troops be transferred for coordinated suppression."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the governors and grand coordinators be pressed to ready provisions; once the wind serves, we can move at once, and I also request land forces to join the campaign."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his request.

sentences.zh: 二十二年六月，瑯自桐山攻克花嶼、貓嶼、草嶼，乘南風進泊八罩。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, sixth month: Lang from Tungshan captured Huayu, Maoyu, and Caoyu, rode the south wind to advance and moored at Bazhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Lang set out from Tungshan, took Huayu, Maoyu, and Caoyu, and rode a south wind to anchor at Bazhao.

sentences.zh: 國軒踞澎湖，緣岸築短牆，置腰銃，環二十餘里為壁壘。

translations.literal: Guoxuan occupied Penghu, built short walls along the shore, placed waist guns, and encircled more than twenty li as fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan held Penghu, building short walls along the shore, posting swivel guns, and ringing more than twenty li of coast with fortifications.

sentences.zh: 瑯遣游擊藍理以鳥船進攻，敵舟乘潮四合。

translations.literal: Lang sent raiding commander Lan Li with swift boats to attack; the enemy ships rode the tide and converged from four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Lang sent the raiding commander Lan Li forward in swift boats, and the enemy ships closed in on the rising tide from every side.

sentences.zh: 瑯乘樓船突入賊陣，流矢傷目，血溢於帕，督戰不少卻，總兵吳英繼之，斬級三千，克虎井、桶盤二嶼。

translations.literal: Lang rode a tower ship and burst into the rebel formation; a stray arrow wounded his eye, blood overflowed onto his handkerchief, yet he directed the battle with little retreat; Commander Wu Ying followed, beheaded three thousand, and captured the two islets of Hujing and Tongpan.
translations.idiomatic: Lang led a tower ship straight into the rebel line; a stray arrow struck his eye and blood soaked his handkerchief, yet he kept directing the fight without yielding. Commander Wu Ying pressed on after him, killing three thousand men and taking the islets of Hujing and Tongpan.

sentences.zh: 旋以百船分列東西，遣總兵陳蟒、魏明、董義、康玉率兵東指雞籠峪、四角山，西指牛心灣，分賊勢。

translations.literal: Soon with a hundred ships divided east and west, he sent commanders Chen Mang, Wei Ming, Dong Yi, and Kang Yu to lead troops east toward Jilongyu and Sijiaoshan and west toward Niuxinwan, dividing the rebel strength.
translations.idiomatic: He then split a hundred ships into eastern and western columns, sending the commanders Chen Mang, Wei Ming, Dong Yi, and Kang Yu east toward Jilongyu and Sijiaoshan and west toward Niuxinwan to divide the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 瑯自督五十六船分八隊，以八十船繼後，揚帆直進。

translations.literal: Lang personally directed fifty-six ships divided into eight squads, with eighty ships following behind, raising sails and advancing straight ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Lang himself led fifty-six ships in eight squadrons, with eighty more following behind, and sailed straight in under full canvas.

sentences.zh: 敵悉眾拒戰，總兵林賢、朱天貴先入陣，天貴戰死。

translations.literal: The enemy mustered all their forces to resist; commanders Lin Xian and Zhu Tianguian entered the formation first, and Tianguian died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy met them with their full strength; the commanders Lin Xian and Zhu Tianguian broke in first, and Tianguian fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 將士奮勇衷擊，自辰至申，焚敵艦百餘，溺死無算，遂取澎湖，國軒遁歸台灣​​。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers fought bravely in direct assault; from the chen hour to the shen hour they burned more than a hundred enemy vessels, and drowned deaths were beyond counting; they then took Penghu, and Guoxuan fled back to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: The men fought on with fierce direct assaults; from mid-morning until late afternoon they burned more than a hundred enemy ships and drowned countless rebels, then took Penghu as Guoxuan fled back to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 克塽大驚，遣使詣軍前乞降，瑯疏陳，上許之。

translations.literal: Ke Shuang was greatly alarmed, sent an envoy to the army front to beg surrender; Lang memorialized this, and the Emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Shuang was terrified and sent an envoy to the front to sue for surrender; Lang reported this, and the Emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 八月，瑯統兵入鹿耳門，至台灣。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Lang commanded troops through Lu'ermen and reached Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Lang led his army through Lu'ermen and reached Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 克塽率屬薙發，迎於水次，繳延平王金印。

translations.literal: Ke Shuang led his followers in shaving their heads, welcomed Lang at the waterside, and surrendered the Prince of Yanping's gold seal.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Shuang came with his followers, shaved their heads in submission, met Lang at the shore, and handed over the Prince of Yanping's gold seal.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，自海道報捷。

translations.literal: Taiwan was pacified; victory was reported by the sea route.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan was pacified, and word of victory was sent back by sea.

sentences.zh: 疏至，正中秋，上賦詩旌瑯功，复授靖海將軍，封靖海侯，世襲罔替，賜御用袍及諸服物。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, it was precisely mid-autumn; the Emperor composed a poem to honor Lang's merit, again appointed him Pacification-of-the-Seas General, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pacifying the Seas with perpetual hereditary succession, and bestowed imperial robes and various garments.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the capital, it was the very heart of autumn. The Emperor composed a poem to celebrate Lang's achievement, reappointed him Pacification-of-the-Seas General, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pacifying the Seas with perpetual hereditary rank, and granted him imperial robes and other gifts of attire.

sentences.zh: 瑯疏辭侯封，乞得如內大臣例賜花翎，部議謂非例，上命毋辭，並如其請賜花翎。

translations.literal: Lang memorialized declining the marquisate, requesting that he might receive a peacock feather as granted to inner court ministers by precedent; the ministry deliberated that this was not precedent; the Emperor ordered that he not decline, and also granted a peacock feather as he had requested.
translations.idiomatic: Lang memorialized to decline the marquisate and asked instead for a peacock feather, as inner court ministers received by custom. The ministry ruled that this was irregular, but the Emperor told him not to refuse the title—and also granted the peacock feather he had requested.

sentences.zh: 遣侍郎蘇拜至福建，與督撫及瑯議善後事。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister Su Bai was dispatched to Fujian to discuss post-campaign arrangements with the governors and Lang.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Vice Minister Su Bai to Fujian to consult with the provincial governors and Lang on how to settle affairs after the conquest.

sentences.zh: 有言宜遷其人、棄其地者，瑯疏言：「明季設澎水標於金門，出汛至澎湖而止。

translations.literal: Some said the people should be relocated and the land abandoned. Lang memorialized: "In the late Ming the Penshui Standard was established at Kinmen, with patrols extending only as far as Penghu.
