translations.idiomatic: Some argued that the population should be moved off the island and the territory abandoned. Lang memorialized in reply: "In the late Ming, the Penshui garrison was posted at Kinmen, and patrols went no farther than Penghu.

sentences.zh: 台灣原屬化外，土番雜處，未入版圖。

translations.literal: Taiwan originally lay beyond civilization, with aboriginal tribes mixed together, not yet entered on the territorial maps.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan had lain outside the civilized order, a land where native tribes mingled, not yet charted within the empire's borders.

sentences.zh: 然其時中國之民潛往生聚，已不下萬人。

translations.literal: Yet even then Chinese subjects secretly went there to gather and settle—already no fewer than ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Even then, however, Chinese settlers had slipped across in secret to live there together—already no fewer than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 鄭芝龍為海寇，據為巢穴。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhilong became a sea bandit and made it his lair.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhilong turned pirate and made the island his stronghold.

sentences.zh: 及崇禎元年，芝龍就撫，借與紅毛為互市之所。

translations.literal: By the first year of Chongzhen, Zhilong submitted to pacification and lent the place to the Dutch as a mutual-trading port.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen, Zhilong accepted imperial pacification and leased the place to the Dutch as a trading port.

sentences.zh: 紅毛聯結土番，招納內地民，漸作邊患。

translations.literal: The Dutch allied with the native tribes, recruited people from the interior, and gradually created a border threat.
translations.idiomatic: The Dutch allied with the native tribes, drew settlers from the mainland, and little by little turned the island into a frontier menace.

sentences.zh: 至順治十八年，鄭成功盤踞其地，糾集亡命，荼毒海疆。

translations.literal: By the eighteenth year of Shunzhi, Zheng Chenggong occupied the territory, gathered fugitive desperadoes, and ravaged the coastal regions.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighteenth year of Shunzhi, Zheng Chenggong had seized the island, mustered desperate fugitives, and poisoned the coast for decades.

sentences.zh: 傳及其孫克塽，積數十年。

translations.literal: The rule passed to his grandson Ke Shuang—accumulating several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Power passed to his grandson Ke Shuang, and so it remained for decades.

sentences.zh: 一旦納土歸命，善後之計，尤宜周詳。

translations.literal: Now that they have surrendered the land and submitted to command, the plans for settlement afterward must be especially thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have surrendered the territory and submitted to the throne, the plans for what comes after must be laid with especial care.

sentences.zh: 若棄其地、遷其人，以有限之船，渡無限之民，非閱數年，難以報竣。

translations.literal: If we abandon the land and relocate the people, using limited ships to ferry unlimited people, it would not be completed within several years.
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon the land and move the people, limited shipping cannot carry an unlimited population—years would pass before the task was finished.

sentences.zh: 倘渡載不盡，竄匿山谷，所謂藉寇兵而齎盜糧也。

translations.literal: If transport could not carry them all and they hid in mountain valleys, that would be what is called borrowing bandit soldiers and carrying robbers' grain.
translations.idiomatic: If not all could be evacuated and the rest hid in the hills, we would be arming the bandits and feeding the robbers.

sentences.zh: 且此地原為紅毛所有，乘隙复踞，必竊窺內地，鼓惑人心。

translations.literal: Moreover, this territory was originally held by the Dutch; if they seized the opening to reoccupy it, they would surely steal glances at the interior and incite men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, this land once belonged to the Dutch. Given the chance to seize it again, they would surely turn covetous eyes inland and stir men's hearts against us.

sentences.zh: 重以夾板船之精堅，海外無敵，沿海諸省，斷難安然無虞。

translations.literal: Add to this the excellence and stoutness of their decked ships, unmatched overseas—the coastal provinces would hardly remain secure and untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Their decked warships are stout and swift, unmatched on the open sea—the coastal provinces could hardly sleep untroubled.

sentences.zh: 至時復勤師遠征，恐未易見效。

translations.literal: If at that time troops were again mobilized for distant expedition, I fear it would not easily achieve effect.
translations.idiomatic: To mobilize the army again for a distant campaign would then be costly—and success far from assured.

sentences.zh: 如僅守澎湖，則孤懸汪洋之中，土地單薄，遠隔金門、廈門，豈不受制於彼，而能一朝居哉？

translations.literal: If we held only Penghu, it would stand isolated in the midst of vast waters, its land meager, far from Kinmen and Xiamen—would it not be controlled by them and unable to endure long?
translations.idiomatic: If we held Penghu alone, it would stand isolated on the open sea—thin soil, far from Kinmen and Xiamen. Would we not be at their mercy, unable to hold it for long?

sentences.zh: 臣思海氛既靖，汰內地溢設之官兵，分防兩處：台灣設總兵一、水師副將一、陸營參將二、兵八千；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that since the maritime troubles are already settled, we should eliminate supernumerary officers and soldiers set up in the interior and distribute defenses to two places: Taiwan—one commander-in-chief, one vice commander of the navy, two brigade commanders of land forces, eight thousand troops;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant proposes that, with the seas now quiet, we trim the excess garrisons inland and redeploy troops to two posts: on Taiwan, one regional commander, one naval vice commander, two land-force brigade commanders, and eight thousand men;

sentences.zh: 澎湖設水師副將一、兵二千。

translations.literal: Penghu—one vice commander of the navy, two thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: on Penghu, one naval vice commander and two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 初無添兵增餉之費，已足固守。

translations.literal: At first there would be no cost of adding troops and increasing pay, yet it would be sufficient to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: At no added cost in troops or pay, the garrisons would suffice to hold both places.

sentences.zh: 其總兵、副將、參、遊等官，定以二三年轉升內地。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief, vice commanders, brigade and patrol officers would be fixed to rotate to interior posts within two or three years.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commanders, vice commanders, brigade officers, and patrol officers would rotate back to mainland posts every two or three years.

sentences.zh: 其地正賦雜糧，暫行蠲豁。

translations.literal: The land tax and miscellany grain of the region would for the time being be remitted and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax and grain levies there would be remitted for the time being.

sentences.zh: 駐兵現給全餉，三年後開徵濟用，即不盡資內地轉輸。

translations.literal: The garrison troops would for now receive full pay; three years later collection would begin to supply needs, thus not wholly relying on transport from the interior.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison would draw full rations at first; after three years local revenue could begin to meet the need, so the mainland would not bear the whole burden of supply.

sentences.zh: 蓋籌天下形勢，必期萬全，台灣雖在外島，關四省要害，斷不可棄。

translations.literal: In planning the empire's strategic posture, one must expect complete security: though Taiwan is an outer island, it concerns the vital points of four provinces—it absolutely must not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In weighing the empire's strategic position, nothing less than complete security will do. Taiwan may be an outer island, but it guards the vital approaches of four provinces—it must not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 並繪圖以進。」

translations.literal: He also submitted maps."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted maps along with the memorial."

sentences.zh: 疏入，下議政王大臣等議，仍未決。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was sent down to the Prince Regent and grand ministers for deliberation; still no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached court, it was referred to the Prince Regent and the grand ministers—but still no decision was made.

sentences.zh: 上召詢廷臣，大學士李霨奏應如瑯請。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned and questioned court ministers; Grand Secretary Li Huo memorialized that Lang's request should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor called in the court ministers for counsel. Grand Secretary Li Huo advised that Lang's proposal should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 尋蘇拜等疏亦用瑯議，並設縣三、府一、巡道一，上命允行。

translations.literal: Soon Su Bai and others also memorialized adopting Lang's plan, and established three counties, one prefecture, and one circuit intendant; the Emperor ordered it approved and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Su Bai and the others memorialized in support of Lang's plan as well, recommending three counties, one prefecture, and one circuit intendant. The Emperor approved, and the arrangement was put into effect.

sentences.zh: 瑯又疏請克塽納土歸誠，應攜族屬與劉國軒、馮錫範及明裔朱桓等俱詣京師，詔授克塽公銜，國軒、錫范伯銜，俱隸上三旗，餘職官及桓等於近省安插墾荒。

translations.literal: Lang also memorialized requesting that since Ke Shuang had surrendered the land in good faith, his clansmen together with Liu Guoxuan, Feng Xifan, and Ming descendant Zhu Huan should all proceed to the capital; an edict appointed Ke Shuang with ducal rank, Guoxuan and Xifan with earl's rank, all assigned to the Upper Three Banners, while remaining officials and Huan were settled to reclaim wasteland in nearby provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Lang also memorialized that, since Ke Shuang had surrendered the territory in good faith, he should come to the capital with his clansmen, Liu Guoxuan, Feng Xifan, and the Ming descendant Zhu Huan. An edict granted Ke Shuang ducal rank and Guoxuan and Xifan the rank of earl; all were enrolled in the Upper Three Banners. The remaining officials and Zhu Huan were resettled in nearby provinces to reclaim wasteland.

sentences.zh: 复疏請申嚴海禁，稽核貿易商船，命如所議。

translations.literal: He again memorialized requesting strict enforcement of the sea ban and inspection of merchant trading vessels; the Emperor ordered as deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again to tighten the sea ban and inspect merchant vessels; the Emperor ordered his proposals carried out.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，入覲，溫旨慰勞，賞賚優渥。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh year: he came to court for audience; warm edicts consoled and praised him, and rewards were generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he came to court. The Emperor received him with warm words of praise and lavished rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 上諭瑯曰：「爾前為內大臣十有三年，當時尚有輕爾者。

translations.literal: The Emperor addressed Lang: "You formerly served as inner court minister for thirteen years; at that time some still looked down on you.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Lang, "You served as an inner court minister for thirteen years, and even then some still looked down on you.

sentences.zh: 惟朕深知爾，待爾甚厚。

translations.literal: Only I knew you deeply and treated you very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Only I knew your worth and treated you with great favor.

sentences.zh: 後三逆平定，惟海寇潛據台灣為福建害，欲除此寇，非爾不可。

translations.literal: After the three rebel lines were pacified, only the sea bandits secretly held Taiwan to harm Fujian; to eliminate these bandits, none but you would do.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Feudatories were crushed, only the sea rebels still held Taiwan and plagued Fujian. To root them out, no one but you would do.

sentences.zh: 朕特加擢用，爾能不負任使，舉六十年難靖之寇，殄滅無餘。

translations.literal: I specially promoted and employed you; you were able not to betray the trust of your commission and annihilated without remnant a banditry sixty years difficult to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: I promoted you expressly for this task, and you did not fail the trust I placed in you—you wiped out a rebellion that had defied pacification for sixty years, leaving not a trace behind.

sentences.zh: 或有言爾恃功驕傲，朕令爾來京。

translations.literal: Some said you relied on merit and were arrogant; I ordered you to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Some said you had grown proud on your laurels, so I summoned you to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又有言當留勿遣者，朕思寇亂之際，尚用爾勿疑，況天下已平，反疑而勿遣耶？

translations.literal: Others said you should be kept and not sent back; I thought that in the midst of bandit turmoil I still employed you without doubt—how much more now that the realm is pacified would I doubt and not send you back?
translations.idiomatic: Others said I ought to keep you here and not send you back. I reasoned that in the midst of rebellion I still trusted you without hesitation—now that the realm is at peace, would I turn suspicious and refuse to let you return?

sentences.zh: 今命爾復任，宜益加敬慎，以保功名。」

translations.literal: Now I appoint you to resume your post; you should be all the more respectful and cautious to preserve your merit and fame."
translations.idiomatic: Now I appoint you to your post again. Be all the more careful and respectful, and preserve the honor you have won."

sentences.zh: 瑯奏謝，言：「臣年力已衰，懼勿勝封疆之重。」

translations.literal: Lang memorialized thanks, saying: "Your servant's years and strength have already declined; I fear I am not equal to the weight of frontier defense."
translations.idiomatic: Lang thanked him and said, "Your servant's years and strength are failing; I fear I am no longer equal to so weighty a frontier command."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「將尚智不尚力。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Generals honor wisdom, not brute strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "A general is valued for wit, not brute strength.

sentences.zh: 朕用爾亦智耳，豈在手足之力哉？」

translations.literal: When I employ you it is for wisdom—is it in the strength of hands and feet?"
translations.idiomatic: I employ you for your mind—what need have I of the strength in your arms and legs?"

sentences.zh: 命還任。

translations.literal: He ordered him to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Lang to return to his command.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，卒於官，年七十六，贈太子少傅，賜祭葬，諡襄壯。

translations.literal: Thirty-fifth year: he died in office at age seventy-six; posthumously conferred Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent, granted sacrificial honors and burial, posthumous name Xiangzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he died in office, aged seventy-six. He was posthumously made Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent, granted state funeral honors, and given the posthumous name Xiangzhuang.

sentences.zh: 瑯治軍嚴整，通陣法。

translations.literal: Lang governed the army with strict discipline and understood battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: Lang kept his troops in strict order and was thoroughly versed in battle formations.

sentences.zh: 尤善水戰，諳海中風候。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at naval warfare and knew sea wind and weather.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled above all at naval warfare and knew the winds and seasons of the open sea.

sentences.zh: 將出師，值光地請急歸，問瑯曰：「眾皆言南風不利，今乃刻六月出師，何也？」

translations.literal: When about to march out, encountering Guangdi's urgent request to return home, he asked Lang: "Everyone says the south wind is unfavorable—why choose the sixth month to march out?"
translations.idiomatic: As the fleet was about to sail, Li Guangdi, who had asked leave to return home in haste, questioned Lang: "Everyone says the south wind is unfavorable—why fix on the sixth month to take the fleet out?"

sentences.zh: 瑯曰：「北風日夜猛。

translations.literal: Lang said: "The north wind is fierce day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Lang replied, "The north wind blows hard day and night.

sentences.zh: 今攻澎湖，未能一戰克。

translations.literal: Now attacking Penghu, we cannot take it in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: If we attack Penghu now, we cannot hope to take it in a single engagement.

sentences.zh: 風起舟散，將何以戰？

translations.literal: When wind rises the fleet scatters—how then shall we fight?
translations.idiomatic: When the wind rises the fleet will scatter—how then are we to fight?

sentences.zh: 夏至前後二十餘日，風微，夜尤靜，可聚泊大洋。

translations.literal: For about twenty-odd days before and after the summer solstice, winds are light and nights especially calm; we can gather and anchor on the open sea.
translations.idiomatic: For some twenty days before and after the summer solstice the winds are mild and the nights especially still—we can mass the fleet and anchor on the open sea.

sentences.zh: 觀釁而動，不過七日，舉之必矣。

translations.literal: Watch for an opening and move; within seven days we will surely take it.
translations.idiomatic: Watch for the right moment and strike; within seven days we are sure to carry it.

sentences.zh: 即偶有颶風，此則天意，非人慮所及。

translations.literal: Even if occasionally a hurricane arises, that is Heaven's intent, beyond human foresight.
translations.idiomatic: If a hurricane should come, that is Heaven's will—not something human planning can forestall.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏將劉國軒最驍，以他將守澎湖，雖敗，彼必再戰。

translations.literal: Liu Guoxuan was the fiercest of the Zheng generals; if another general held Penghu, though defeated they would surely fight again.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guoxuan was the fiercest of the Zheng commanders. If some other general held Penghu, defeat would only bring another battle.

sentences.zh: 今以國軒守，敗則膽落，台灣可​​不戰而下。」

translations.literal: Now with Guoxuan holding it, once defeated their courage will sink and Taiwan can be taken without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: With Guoxuan in command, one defeat will break their nerve—and Taiwan will fall without another fight."

sentences.zh: 及戰，雲起東南，國軒望見，謂颶作，喜甚。

translations.literal: When battle came, clouds rose in the southeast; Guoxuan saw them and, thinking a hurricane was forming, was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: When battle came, clouds piled up in the southeast. Guoxuan saw them, took them for the onset of a hurricane, and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 俄，雷聲殷殷，國軒推案起曰：「天命矣！

translations.literal: Suddenly thunder rolled deeply; Guoxuan pushed back from the table and rose, saying: "Heaven's mandate!
translations.idiomatic: Then thunder rolled across the sky. Guoxuan shoved back from his desk and rose, crying, "Heaven has spoken!

sentences.zh: 今且敗。」

translations.literal: Now we shall be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: We are lost today."

sentences.zh: 人謂瑯必報父仇，將致毒於鄭氏。

translations.literal: People said Lang would surely avenge his father's death and bring ruin upon the Zheng clan.
translations.idiomatic: People expected Lang to avenge his father's death and visit ruin on the Zheng clan.

sentences.zh: 瑯曰：「絕島新附，一有誅戮，恐人情反側。

translations.literal: Lang said: "The isolated island has newly submitted; the least execution would fear people's hearts turning unstable.
translations.idiomatic: Lang said, "The island has only just submitted. The least bloodshed would set hearts churning.

sentences.zh: 吾所以銜卹茹痛者，為國事重，不敢顧私也。」

translations.literal: The reason I held grief in my mouth and swallowed pain was that state affairs weighed heavily—I dared not look to private matters."
translations.idiomatic: I swallowed my grief for the sake of the state—I dared not indulge private vengeance."

sentences.zh: 子世綸、世驃，自有傳；

translations.literal: His sons Shilun and Shipiao have their own biographies;
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shilun and Shipiao have biographies of their own;

sentences.zh: 世範，襲爵。

translations.literal: Shifan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 朱天貴，福建莆田人。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianguai—Zhu Tianguai was a man of Putian in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianguai came from Putian in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 初為鄭錦將。

translations.literal: At first he was a general under Zheng Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as a general under Zheng Jing.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，師下海壇，以所部二萬人、舟三百來降，授平陽總兵。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year of Kangxi: when the army descended on Haitan, he came to surrender with twenty thousand men under his command and three hundred boats; he was appointed commander at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi, when the imperial fleet descended on Haitan, he surrendered with twenty thousand men and three hundred vessels under his command and was made regional commander at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 瑯攻澎湖，天貴以師會。

translations.literal: When Lang attacked Penghu, Tianguai joined forces with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang attacked Penghu, Tianguai brought his troops to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 國軒拒戰，天貴以十二舟薄敵壘，焚其舟，殺傷甚眾，戰益力，俄，中飛砲僕舟中，猶大呼殺賊，遂卒，贈太子少保，諡忠壯。

translations.literal: Guoxuan resisted in battle; Tianguai with twelve boats pressed close to the enemy ramparts, burned their vessels, killed and wounded very many, fought all the harder; suddenly he was struck by a flying cannon, fell in the boat, yet still cried loudly to kill the bandits, and then died; posthumously conferred Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan resisted fiercely. Tianguai closed on the enemy works with twelve boats, set their ships afire, and killed or wounded a great many. He fought all the harder until a cannonball struck him down in his vessel; even then he shouted to kill the rebels before he died. He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：台灣平，瑯專其功。

translations.literal: Commentary: The commentators say: When Taiwan was pacified, Lang monopolized the credit.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: When Taiwan was pacified, Lang took the lion's share of the credit.

sentences.zh: 然啟聖、興祚經營規畫，戡定諸郡縣。

translations.literal: Yet Qisheng and Xingzuo had laid the plans and arrangements and subjugated the various prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yao Qisheng and Wu Xingzuo had laid the groundwork, planned the campaign, and brought the coastal prefectures and counties to heel.

sentences.zh: 及金、廈既下，鄭氏僅有台澎，遂聚而殲。

translations.literal: Once Kinmen and Xiamen had fallen, the Zheng clan held only Taiwan and Penghu—then they were gathered together and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kinmen and Xiamen had fallen, the Zheng held only Taiwan and Penghu—and then they were cornered and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 先事之勞，何可泯也？

translations.literal: How can the labor of prior preparation be erased?
translations.idiomatic: How can the work done beforehand be erased from the record?

sentences.zh: 及瑯出師，啟聖、興祚欲與同進，瑯遽疏言未奉督撫同進之命。

translations.literal: When Lang marched out, Qisheng and Xingzuo wished to advance together; Lang hurriedly memorialized that he had received no order for the governors to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang took the fleet out, Qisheng and Xingzuo wished to advance with him—but Lang hastily memorialized that he had received no order for the governors to join the expedition.

sentences.zh: 上命啟聖同瑯進取，止興祚毋行。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Qisheng to advance with Lang to seize [Taiwan], but stopped Xingzuo from going.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Qisheng to advance with Lang, but barred Xingzuo from going.

sentences.zh: 既克，啟聖告捷疏後瑯至，賞不及，鬱鬱發病卒。

translations.literal: After the conquest, Qisheng's victory memorial arrived after Lang's; rewards did not reach him—he fell ill from dejection and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory, Qisheng's report of triumph reached court after Lang's—and the rewards never reached him. He sickened from grief and died.

sentences.zh: 功名之際，有難言之矣。

translations.literal: At the juncture of merit and fame, there were things hard to speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: At the crossroads of merit and fame, there are things one can hardly put into words.

sentences.zh: 大敵在前，將帥內相競，審擇堅任，一戰而克。

translations.literal: With the great enemy before them, generals competed inwardly among themselves; [the Emperor] carefully chose and firmly entrusted—one battle and victory.
translations.idiomatic: With a formidable enemy before them and rivalry among the commanders within, the Emperor chose his man with care, entrusted him firmly, and won in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 非聖祖善馭群材，曷能有此哉？

translations.literal: Had it not been for the Sage Ancestor's skill in managing diverse talents, how could there have been this?
translations.idiomatic: Had the Sage Ancestor not known so well how to harness the talents of many men, how could such an outcome have been achieved?
